name: Mangrove
notes: Intertidal salt-tolerant forest: stilt-rooted Rhizophora on the seaward edge, pneumatophore-bearing Avicennia/Sonneratia, Laguncularia/Bruguiera landward, nipa palm and ferns at the freshwater fringe. Drawn on the Atlantic-East Pacific (Florida, Caribbean, W Africa) and Indo-West Pacific (Sundarbans, SE Asia, N Australia) mangrove provinces.

canopy.name: Coconut palm

growth.juvenile_note: The husked nut lies on the sand and after 2-6 months a pointed shoot pushes out of one end while the nut's flesh feeds the seedling. First leaves are entire, stiff, strap-like blades split only at the tip (bifid), in a stemless fan-like rosette; pinnate fronds come later, and a trunk rises after ~3-5 years, widening from a bulbous base ('bole').
growth.source: Wikipedia Coconut (tall palms bear at 6-10 yr, live 60-100 yr; ~11 months from female flower opening to harvest; up to 15 inflorescences/yr; ~80 nuts/yr, up to 150; nut ~1.4 kg; largely cross-pollinated, dwarfs selfing); ICRAF Agroforestree (tall selections 24-30 m, flowers after ~6th yr); germination from FAO coconut guides

canopy.source: Palm of tropical coasts worldwide; height 15-30 m. Leaning trunk, feather crown; sea-dispersed nuts. Standard floras and Kew POWO for the name.

bark.note: swollen yellow-green pseudobulb canes with papery sheaths at the nodes

growth.juvenile_note: Dust-like seed lodges in bark and, with a fungal partner, swells into a tiny green protocorm that sprouts roots and a first leaf over months. The young plant is a small tuft of thin stems with two ranks of short, fleshy, oblong leaves; stems thicken into pseudobulbs at the base and lengthen each year into a clump of cane-like stems, the older ones leafless and flowering.
growth.source: Wikipedia Dendrobium crumenatum (sympodial epiphyte; stems 30-70 cm, swollen at lower nodes; leaves in two ranks; exposed lowland forest and coastal scrub; flowers 9 days after a >5.5 C temperature drop, all at once, lasting one day). Seedling timings and lifespan estimated from Dendrobium culture.

epiphyte.name: Strangler fig

growth.juvenile_note: Usually starts as a bird-dropped seed in a palm boot or branch fork: a tiny leafy shrublet perched on the host, with glossy oval leaves, that sends thin aerial roots down the trunk. Once they reach soil the roots thicken and fuse into a lattice that strangles the host; it can also start on the ground or on rocks as a normal sapling.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Ficus aurea: hemiepiphytic strangler to 30 m that germinates in the host canopy; fast-growing). Germination, ages and lifespan estimated from Ficus.

epiphyte.source: Florida and Caribbean hammocks. Starts in a crown, sends roots down, kills the host — a real strangler event on old trees. Kew POWO.
